title: TrailGenic Overextension Fasted Hiking Safety Dataset
description: Fasted high-load hiking was sustainable under normal cadence, but the compressed Western Altitude Block exceeded the recovery envelope. This does not diagnose overtraining syndrome and does not prove fasting caused recovery failure; sleep, cadence, travel, altitude, duration, and cumulative load are emphasized.

records.mechanism: Western Altitude Block update through Wheeler Peak
physiological_response: Fasted high-load hiking was sustainable under normal cadence, but the compressed Western Altitude Block exceeded the recovery envelope. This does not diagnose overtraining syndrome and does not prove fasting caused recovery failure; sleep, cadence, travel, altitude, duration, and cumulative load are emphasized.
adaptation_outcomes: The adaptation remained; the compressed block exceeded the current recovery envelope.

records.mechanism: Twenty-two fasted high-load hikes show absorbed rather than accumulated load when recovery architecture is intact

stimulus.apex_session: San Gorgonio via Vivian Creek, May 9, 2026

physiological_response: No overreaching pattern emerged across 22 high-load fasted hiking sessions.
Seven consecutive Day-2 AUTONOMIC_RESTORED reads indicate load was absorbed rather than accumulated.
Even after the apex San Gorgonio effort, Day-2 HRV rebounded to 54 ms from a 23 ms pre-hike state.
adaptation_outcomes: Fasted high-load hiking is sustainable in this protocol when sleep, electrolytes, pacing, and recovery monitoring are maintained.
Day-2 supercompensation becomes the safety signal separating adaptation from overextension.
Compressed pre-hike sleep remains a Day-1 risk modifier even when Day-2 recovery is robust.

supporting_science.finding: Overtraining risk is best interpreted through performance and recovery markers across time, not single-session load alone.
Fueling and intensity management shape the risk profile of prolonged endurance work.

records.mechanism: Hypoglycemia risk during prolonged fasted endurance activity
physiological_response: increased reliance on hepatic glucose production
adaptation_outcomes: development of pacing discipline during fasted endurance activity
improved metabolic resilience when training stress is managed appropriately

supporting_science.finding: Prolonged endurance activity without adequate carbohydrate availability increases risk of hypoglycemia and fatigue.

records.mechanism: Excessive cortisol and stress response from prolonged energy deficit
adaptation_outcomes: recognition of safe duration limits for fasted endurance activity
improved balance between metabolic stress and recovery

supporting_science.finding: Prolonged endurance exercise can elevate cortisol levels and increase physiological stress responses.

records.mechanism: Dehydration and electrolyte imbalance during fasted endurance exposure
adaptation_outcomes: integration of electrolyte strategies during fasted endurance training
greater physiological stability during long-duration efforts

supporting_science.finding: Fluid and electrolyte balance are critical for maintaining physiological stability during prolonged endurance exercise.

records.mechanism: Overtraining risk from repeated high-duration fasted endurance sessions
adaptation_outcomes: development of sustainable endurance training strategies

supporting_science.finding: Insufficient recovery between endurance sessions can lead to overtraining syndrome and impaired physiological adaptation.

western_altitude_block_summary.interpretation: Normal cadence usually restored; compressed summit stacking exposed the current recovery boundary.
